chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When one of you feels soft-hearted, let him supplicate, for the heart does not soften until it is sincere.

key_terms.الْقَلْبَ: The heart; in this context, the spiritual center of understanding and emotion.
key_terms.رَقَّ: To feel soft-hearted or tender; to have one's heart softened by emotion or divine grace.
key_terms.يَخْلُصَ: To become pure, sincere, or free from impurities/distractions.
key_terms.يَدْعُ: To supplicate or call upon God (dua).

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the heart to soften and accept supplication according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical sensation of heart softening (raqqa) to the spiritual necessity of sincerity (ikhlas), teaching that supplication is most potent when the heart is purified from worldly distractions. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on the internal state of the supplicant, where emotional receptivity serves as a divine sign that the heart has become a clear vessel for divine response. It highlights the interplay between spiritual preparation and the timing of dua, suggesting that such moments are opportunities for deepening one's connection with Allah through pure devotion.
